s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement and discomfort of a digit with associated neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been larger than the others since birth
The finger has grown progressively over time
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
The patient has limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
There is no history of trauma
There is no history of fever, weight loss, or appetite change
The overlying skin of the enlarged finger is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
The temperature of the affected area is normal
Sensation is decreased distally
Resistance to flexion prevents full finger flexion
Laboratory studies are unremarkable
A CT scan of the hand shows overgrowth of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges plus surrounding soft tissue

shortlist.label: Macrodactyly
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive enlargement of the finger since birth

shortlist.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showing overgrowth of phalanges and soft tissue, suggesting a lipomatous process

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to lipofibromatous hamartoma, with possible association with nerve compression

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible explanation for progressive enlargement and associated neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, still a possible cause of progressive enlargement and neurological symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's condition is characterized by progressive enlargement of the left middle finger since birth, which is a key feature of macrodactyly. The CT scan showing overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: While the CT scan suggests a lipomatous process, lipofibromatous hamartoma typically presents with a different set of symptoms and is less likely to cause progressive enlargement of the finger.

rejected.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Similar to lipofibromatous hamartoma, fibrolipomatous hamartoma is less likely to cause the progressive enlargement seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with a triad of port-wine stain, varicose veins, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
rejected.why: While neurofibromatosis type 1 can cause soft tissue tumors, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with macrodactyly.
